policyBasis: CONTRIBUTING.md: "Strapi is using GitHub issues to manage bugs. We keep a close eye on them. Before filing a new issue, try to ensure your problem does not already exist." .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml sets blank_issues_enabled: false, so the report must go through BUG_REPORT.yml, whose required fields are Node version, package manager + version, exact Strapi version ("Latest" is not a valid response), OS, database, JS/TS, Bug Description, Steps to Reproduce, Expected Behavior, and both confirmation checkboxes.
notes: File this on strapi/strapi, not strapi/documentation: the wrong number is inside the shipped product (input-schemas.ts:33 is what a client reads in tools/list), so the docs are downstream of the code and would only need editing if maintainers decide 10 is the intended default. Two supporting facts worth including because they close off the easy dismissals: the 10 is hardcoded in packages/core/utils/src/pagination.ts and unreachable by config, so no app setting explains it; and the MCP unit tests are green on 25 only because they mock documentManager.findPage and hardcode pagination: { page: 1, pageSize: 25 } in the mock's return value (mcp/__tests__/derive-content-type-mcp-tools.test.ts:128-133, 625-633), i.e. they assert the mock. Secondary observation for the same issue: the schema's max of 100 is enforced by Zod at the tool boundary while findPage passes maxLimit 1000, so the two ceilings disagree (the tighter one wins). Note also that the scenario aborted at the first failing step, so the max-100 and page-2 assertions never ran and are untested rather than passing.
